facts.text: Eau Claire’s name comes from a clear stream, French “eau claire,” chosen by early settler Henry Rush after the Potawatomi land.
The village was officially founded in 1861 when William Smythe Farmer opened the first post office and Henry Rush became postmaster.
In 1882 the railroad arrived, spurring growth and bringing a cider mill, drug store, hotel, manufacturing plant, and stove company.
Every year since 1974, the International Cherry Pit‑Spitting Championship has been held at Tree‑Mendus Fruit Farm, making Eau Claire a quirky cherry‑spitting capital.
The only drive‑in theater in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, the Star Theatre in nearby Brooklyn, once served the Eau Claire area, reflecting early 20th‑century entertainment.
The village sits partly in Pipestone Township and partly in Berrien Charter Township, illustrating its spread across two local governments.
